newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt not certain to bring forward 98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt not certain to bring forward 98 budget.

text.p: Italy's governing centre-left coalition has not yet decided whether to proceed with a proposal by Prime Minister Romano Prodi to bring forward passage of the 1998 budget, a senior coalition politician said on Wednesday.
Cesare Salvi, leader in the Senate (upper house) of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), said in an interview for Reuters Financial Television that two options were under consideration.

One was to draw up a mini-budget in March for 1997 and present the 1998 budget to parliament on normal schedule in September, the other was to bring forward presentation of the 1998 budget to April or May, Salvi said.

Prodi proposed last month bringing forward passage of the 1998 budget to convince Italy's European Union partners that it was serious about structural reform to its finances in time for planned economic and monetary union (EMU).

Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi, who has offered co-operation if the package includes welfare spending reform, alleged on Wednesday that the government was backing away from the idea of an early 1998 budget.
"It has not yet been decided," Salvi said. "There are two options: either bring forward the (1998) budget to April or May, or draft a mini-budget in March and the budget in September."

Prodi has said he will draw up a mini-budget of spending cuts for 1997 if needed following a deficit overshoot in 1996. He has said he will decide on the basis of official accounts for the last quarter of 1996. Salvi said the accounts would be ready early in March.
The annual budget is usually presented to parliament by September 30 and must be approved by December 31.
